column1: # standard-coverage.tsv (harbor#978) — what bin/standard-inventory.sh coverage needs to know and cannot derive.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A rule with no data judges nothing and says nothing: name-note-create shipped with no
# name-create.d on the box and never fired (measured 2026-11-13). Which file each installed context rule reads is in its
# script, not in a field the engine knows, so it is declared here once. And a PATH tool is "home" when a registered repo
# holds its bytes; the package managers that legitimately put tools on PATH from outside every repo are declared here too.
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> kind <TAB> path <TAB> header <TAB> note
#   id      rule-data: the context rule's id, its file context-rules/user/<id>.md in the config dir (judged only when installed)
#   path    rule-data: the data the rule reads, a glob allowed in the last segment; {cfg} the config dir, {rules} its
#           tool-origin: a folder prefix under {home}; a PATH tool resolving inside it is that manager's, not ours
#   header  row when each data file opens with a header row that is not data; none otherwise; - for a tool-origin
#   note    the fix when the data is missing or empty, or what the origin is
